transcript: Last night, I was invited to a brand new play at Theaterlab called Loneliness Was A Pandemic by Olivia Haller. It's about a dystopian future where robots have become so advanced and self-sufficient that they've pretty much destroyed humanity, only sparing a few people that they intend to learn how to make art from. Our main character, Human 1, is assigned to teach Robot 1 how to paint. From this premise, plenty of questions arise around the limits of technology, creativity as a pillar of humanity, free will vs programmatic behavior, and more. So this is definitely an “idea play” but Emily Sullivan as Human 1 delivers a really great performance and provides a strong emotional core to the story. This play had me thinking about how technology was intended to connect us, but it has arguably isolated us more than anything else. In the age of AI, there are a lot of new plays being written about technology vs humanity, and this is definitely one of the more successful pieces I've seen that fall into that camp. If this sounds up your alley, Loneliness Was A Pandemic is running through November 24th at Theaterlab. With that, other program for my collection.
